messages:
alex: Hey team — trying to land my initial change (small refactor in services/auth). Two quick q's: 1) which branch should I target for a tiny fix (main vs stable/2026.03)? 2) what's the PR body checklist we should follow (linked issue, perf note, etc.)? Ran into a flaky test locally. Commands I used:
```bash
git checkout -b feat/auth-refactor
# make changes
git commit -am "cleanup: ephemeral auth refactor"
git push origin feat/auth-refactor
```
Who usually reviews auth-area PRs? @maya @simon — thanks!

maya: welcome aboard! :tada: For small fixes target `main` unless it's a customer-facing backport. PR body should include: linked ticket (GH-####), one-line summary, what changed, and a checklist: run `make test`, `make lint`, and confirm perf smoke if relevant. Branches: `feat/` or `fix/` prefixes. Avoid `#skip-e2e` unless you really mean it.

alex: got it, thanks. The failing test is `TestAuthTokenExpiry` locally — anyone seen that flake before?

simon: olivia can chime in on flakes, but try running it specifically and with retries: `go test ./services/auth -run TestAuthTokenExpiry -count=5 -v`. We typically squash for small single-file fixes. Also include `CHANGELOG: none` in PR body if it's internal.

olivia: we see that one occasionally on mac builders. It's a timing race. Try reproducing with `-count=20` and if it still fails, add a short wait or make timing deterministic. If CI still flakes after your push, ping me and I'll take a look.

jr-bot: CI: build queued — https://ci.redwood.ai/builds/12345 (triggered by alex/feat/auth-refactor)

alex: cool — I'll rerun tests locally and push a tweak. One more: do we need CODEOWNERS approval for `services/auth/*`?

maya: yes, `services/auth/*` is owned by `@auth-team` per CODEOWNERS. Add them as reviewers or mention `@auth-team` in the PR description and that should be fine.

alex: perfect, adding reviewers. Appreciate the quick help :pray:
